about.text: A milk pudding of the Middle East made by boiling milk with sugar and thickening it with rice flour, starch or semolina; it was in Arab and Persian cookbooks by the 10th century.

facts.v: Rose or orange-flower water, mastic, pistachio
10th century: thickened milk with ground rice, milk with rice grains and chicken, and an egg custard; an Ottoman recipe of 1530 is meatless, with rose water
In Egypt, mahalabiya is set in a large batch during Ramadan, cut into pieces, and served with honey, chopped nuts and Qamar al-Din apricot paste
Used as the custard in galaktoboureko, flavoured with lemon, orange or rose; the name is Turkish, shared across Greece and Turkey
